item.description: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) makes a catch during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New England Patriots wide receiver AJ Brown has now practiced for three consecutive days leading up to the Pats' game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning. However, he is still listed as questionable due to knee and ankle injuries. A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) practiced Friday for a third straight day. Via @MikeReiss pic.twitter.com/PCRf28UZdX - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) November 13, 2026 The fact that he even made the trip to Munich is a promising sign, but we would still consider him to be truly questionable for Sunday's game. In the worst-case scenario, we would expect Brown to return in Week 12 after the Patriots' Week 11 bye, but hopefully he's able to go this week. We view him as being on the right side of questionable. Fantasy Impact WR AJ Brown, New England Patriots Getting Brown in their lineup would be a huge boost for fantasy owners, especially in a favorable matchup against the Detroit Lions. Their secondary has been battered all season, and they have struggled mightily against the pass. We are putting Brown right back in our lineups this week if he's active. Since getting injured in Week 1, we have viewed Brown as a potential league-winner down the stretch. That's exactly what we are still expecting from Brown during this last push towards the fantasy playoffs. WR DeMario Douglas, New England Patriots Douglas has helped carry a ton of fantasy teams over the past month or so, but he becomes very risky if the Pats have both Brown and Mack Hollins back on the field. That's not to say that he can't have a big game, but his production will become much more erratic. It's something we have seen throughout his entire stint in New England. He will be a risky flex option if Brown is active. QB Drake Maye, New England Patriots After a terrible first few weeks of the season, Maye has been the high-end QB1 fantasy owners thought they were getting when they drafted him. That's without us ever seeing him with his full complement of weapons. This could be the closest we've gotten if Brown is able to return this week. No team has given up more fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. He should have a monster week overseas if he finally has his top target back and healthy. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Freiburg duo discuss national team life ahead of Germany's Serbia test
item.description: Freiburg duo discuss national team life ahead of Germany's Serbia test Germany’s final international break of 2026 sees Jürgen Klopp’s charges visit Serbia tonight before hosting the Netherlands on Monday. Sitting on five points after four outings, this year’s UEFA Nations League campaign hangs in the balance and even a positive result in Belgrade will only force an all-important decider. Trailing both the Netherlands and Greece by three points, Germany are in desperate need of a win against Serbia in tonight’s encounter ahead of their final match at the Olympiastadion. SC Freiburg’s Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant took up media duties, with the former touching on his development while the latter discussed his 24th birthday celebrations with the national team just three days ago. On initially being welcomed into the fold, Treu was full of praise for familiar faces, singling out Nico Schlotterbeck in particular: “One thing that really helped me at the start was already knowing quite a few of the players.” As one of the relatively new additions, Treu also faced a dilemma on what to do with his debut shirt: “It caused quite a stir, even at home (laughs). My girlfriend and I have agreed that it can go on the rail at home where I keep my most special shirts.” In terms of matters on the pitch, attention then turned to the full-back’s playing style: “Moving to SC Freiburg has really helped me because I’m getting more opportunities to get involved in the final third. That’s been hugely beneficial in terms of improving my attacking play.” Determined to provide an outlet on the flank, Treu expressed his desire to make a difference during this camp: “I want to offer even more of a goal threat in the next two games.” With the Serbian federation currently being punished for a number of discriminatory incidents, tonight’s match will have a slightly different feel. On playing behind closed doors, Treu naturally expressed his disappointment: “It’s obviously a shame because every footballer wants to play in front of fans.” Drawing on his experience from the pandemic and trying to see the positive side, he reassuringly added: “One possible advantage is that we’ll be able to communicate even better on the pitch. But overall, the circumstances won’t make much difference to us.” Scherhant, who also earned his first international call-up in September, celebrated another important milestone with the team on Tuesday: “The team sang for me, in several different languages too.” Adopting a slightly more serious tone, he added: “But I’ve already received the best birthday present I could ask for, which is being here with the national team.” Despite the task at hand in Belgrade, the young forward was asked about potentially representing Germany at the Olympiastadion on Monday, offering up this very sincere response: “That would be an incredibly special moment for me. item.title: Ball State football coach Mike Uremovich takes blame for ugly Buffalo loss
item.description: MUNCIE — Six times, Ball State 's offense had the ball inside Buffalo's 30-yard line. Six times, Ball State's offense came away with zero points. Ball State football was officially eliminated from bowl game contention with its seventh loss, falling 28-7 to Buffalo at home on Wednesday, Nov. 11 , in a rain-soaked midweek MACtion game. The Cardinals (3-7, 2-4 MAC) scored the first touchdown of the game after recovering a blocked punt in the end zone, then proceeded to score nothing else as the offense fell flat time and time again. More: Three takeaways from Ball State football's miserable loss to Buffalo Ball State head coach Mike Uremovich knew exactly where to place the blame for the offensive failures. "The loss falls on one person, and that's me," Uremovich said Wednesday. "I'm the offensive coordinator. I call the plays. We didn't score a touchdown, that's completely my fault. ... When you get down in the redzone and have to settle for field goals, I'm not calling the right plays, so if you're looking for somebody to blame for this game and the way it ended up at the end, you're looking at him." Despite taking the blame for Wednesday's loss, Uremovich will continue to serve as the offensive play caller. He told the media at Ball State's weekly pregame press conference on Friday, Nov. 13, that he had not considered making a change with play calling. "We're going to continue to do it exactly the way we've done it," Uremovich said. "I've got to do a better job in the red zone, and we have to execute better in the red zone. We moved the ball up and down the field, we spent a lot of time on their end of the field, a lot of time in the red zone and didn't get any points out of it." Where it went wrong on offense for Ball State vs. Buffalo The shortcomings started early. Ball State's first offensive drive made it all the way to Buffalo's 25-yard line before a fourth-and-2 pass attempt by Keldric Luster was swatted at the line. It was the first of three missed field goals for Boehm, each one closer than the last. He missed wide right from 44 yards out with a much cleaner hold just before halftime, then missed wide left from 39 yards away early in the fourth quarter with another off snap. item.title: Giants’ Cam Skattebo calls out MetLife crowd after crushing loss
item.description: Giants running back Cam Skattebo had a rather eventful Thursday night. It ultimately ended in shocking disappointment, as the Giants blew a four-point lead in the final two minutes and lost 24-21 to the Commanders. This was a big-time missed opportunity for the Giants, who now don’t have the NFC East tiebreaker advantage over the Commanders. While the 5-3-1 Giants remain alone atop the division, they could have emerged from Thursday with a significant cushion as their schedule gets tougher. As for Skattebo, he wants to see — and hear — more from the crowd at MetLife Stadium, starting with next week’s home game against the imposing Jaguars. That nationally televised 4:25 p.m. game now looms large. There were some empty seats in the upper deck at MetLife on Thursday night. Skattebo noticed. “Everyone expected a thunderstorm and a dumping-rain game, so probably missing a couple people out there [because of that],” Skattebo said of the vibe. “But it turned out good, man. A lot of people on third down, making noise. I think this stadium could be a little bit louder when the defense is on the field at times in more critical moments. But at the end of the day, we’ve got to execute.” Yes, indeed. The Giants got the ball back with 2:15 left, up 21-17, on Washington’s 46 after an interception. This was the offense’s chance to seal the victory. “We wanted to end the game right there,” right guard Francis Mauigoa told NJ.com. But they went three plays and out, gaining just 5 yards in 29 seconds. A rare terrible punt from Jordan Stout (12 yards) gave the Commanders possession at their 29. They answered with the 71-yard, game-winning touchdown drive. “We had opportunities at the end of the game to close it out — and we didn’t,” Skattebo said. “We’ve just got to execute better.” Skattebo mostly played well after Giants coach John Harbaugh opted to not trade for Jonathan Taylor to replace him. He also had an ill-advised pregame meal that resulted in him puking after the first quarter. “I had a pretzel-wrapped hot dog, didn’t sit right in my stomach, nothing crazy,” he said. “Got rid of it and felt good after.” A pretzel-wrapped hot dog before playing an NFL game? Skattebo just shrugged. item.title: Ravens update QB Lamar Jackson’s status after successful thumb surgery
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens takes the field for warmups prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens released a statement from head coach Jesse Minter on Friday morning that delivered the team’s first rough timeline on Lamar Jackson’s return from a thumb injury suffered 0n November 1. Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8. Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season. The statement is the most concrete update on Jackson’s status since he went down two weeks ago in Buffalo. However, it lacks the following information: Has Jackson undergone surgery on his thumb? If so, when? If not, when will he get surgery on his thumb? Is the given timeline based on when he suffered the injury, when the statement was released, or when he undergoes surgery? The first three questions were subsequently answered by ESPN’s Jamison Hensley and The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec, who both reported that Jackson has undergone surgery and is currently in the rehab process. It is somewhat baffling why the Ravens would not include that information in their statement. Presumably, the beat reporters who confirmed the surgery received their information from a team source. Why, then, couldn’t the team just say that Jackson had undergone successful surgery? Giving a precise date is not even necessary – the type of thing fans and media would love to know, but do not really need to. This story will be updated with more information.

item.title: AC Milan emerge as potential destination for Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk on a free transfer
item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport AC Milan are reportedly monitoring Virgil van Dijk's situation at Liverpool as the veteran defender nears the end of his current contract. The Netherlands international could become one of the most high-profile free agents on the market if he fails to agree on an extension with the Premier League side. Rossoneri monitor contract stand-off at Anfield The future of Van Dijk remains a significant talking point as he enters the final stretch of his tenure with Liverpool. According to reports from La Gazzetta dello Sport, the Rossoneri have held a long-standing interest in the former Southampton man. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and senior advisor Zlatan Ibrahimovic are both understood to be huge admirers of the defender's leadership and technical quality. The connection between the two clubs is further strengthened by Cardinale's RedBird Capital Partners, which maintains a minority stake in Liverpool's parent company, Fenway Sports Group. Despite this interest, any potential move to the San Siro remains contingent on Van Dijk arriving without a transfer fee. Given the player's age and the significant salary he currently commands in England, the Italian giants are only prepared to facilitate a deal on a free transfer. Van Dijk addresses his uncertain future The player himself has remained coy regarding where he will be playing his football next season . Following a recent Premier League clash against Crystal Palace, Van Dijk provided an update on his mindset regarding the situation. 'Let's see what the season brings. I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else,' the captain stated. While Milan offer a chance to remain at the pinnacle of European football, they face stiff competition from suitors outside the continent. The Italian outlet admits that if Van Dijk prioritises one final lucrative payday at this stage of his career, the Rossoneri will struggle to fend off wealthy rivals from Saudi Arabia and Turkey, including Fenerbahce and Galatasaray. However, should the Dutchman wish to keep competing at the highest possible level, San Siro could prove an ideal destination, particularly if Milan secure qualification for next season's Champions League. item.title: Badgers firing on all cylinders ahead of visit from Ohio State
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - APRIL 11: Forward Gavin Morrissey #7 of the Wisconsin Badgers shoots the puck during the NCAA Division I Men's Ice Hockey Championship game between Wisconsin Badgers and Denver Pioneers on April 11, 2026, at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers men’s hockey team is out to one of their best starts in program history, and certainly their best start in the 21st century after earning a shootout win and a 6-0 shutout over the Gophers last weekend. They sit atop the rankings for the second consecutive week while awaiting a visit from Ohio State this weekend. But before we get into Ohio State, let’s revisit last weekend’s trip to Minneapolis, shall we? No. 1 Wisconsin (7-0-1, 3-0-1 Big Ten) is cruising behind their two-headed monster in goal. Sophomores Alexis Cournoyer and Daniel Hauser are both benefiting from the timeshare in the crease, as the Badgers have posted three shutouts so far this season (four if you include the exhibition against Western Michigan). They’ve allowed just six goals since the start of the season. Cournoyer only conceded one goal against the Gophers, and it was in the waning seconds of a five-minute power play after Grady Deering was ejected for boarding in the first period. Wisconsin found the equalizer, and Cournoyer was a perfect three-for-three in the shootout to earn the extra point in the conference standings. Hauser blanked Minnesota on Saturday night for his second shutout of the season, the first road shutout against Minnesota in 16 years. Through four starts, Hauser is now allowing just 0.50 goals per game, a steep decline from his counterpart, Cournoyer, who is allowing a whopping 0.98 goals per game in his four starts. The Badger defensemen also get a good chunk of the credit. After the Gophers struck first on Friday, Wisconsin only allowed seven shot attempts over the final 45 minutes. Hauser faced just 24 shot attempts Saturday. As good as the defense and goaltending have been, the offense is really starting to hum as well. Wisconsin is averaging just shy of five goals per game, having now eclipsed the six-goal threshold in three of their last four games. item.title: Eagles down to 4 captains after starting the season with 7
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles started the 2026 NFL season having voted seven players as captains , and as we enter Week 10, the team’s bye, they are down to just four on the active roster. It’s remarkable how different this team looks halfway through the current campaign. Lane Johnson — Retired Jalen Hurts — Out indefinitely due to blood clots Jordan Davis — Traded to the Jaguars Three of the four remaining captains have had to show their leadership from the sidelines at many points this season, and been unable to contribute on the field. DeVonta Smith — Played in only 4 games, and hasn’t seen the field since Week 6. Saquon Barkley — Missed 2 games due to injury and returned in Week 7 on a pitch count. He suffered a new back injury early in his return, and has been on a closely monitored snap count in the weeks since. Zack Baun — Missed 1 game with a concussion. That leaves just Jordan Mailata as the only captain still on the Eagles active roster to have played in all nine of the team’s games ( and every single offensive snap! ) in 2026. The All-Pro left tackle’s voice and presence is more important than ever with the offensive line turning to younger, inexperienced players up front, and the group falling to one of the worst in the league. This season has been a huge disappointment, with the Eagles heading into their bye week riding a seven-game losing streak. Both sides of the ball have dealt with a long list of injuries, and there’s been little-to-no consistency on offense to allow for the new scheme to develop. The seven players voted as captains at the start of the season were picked by their teammates for a reason, and their leadership was expected to help shepherd a new system in Philly, but instead, the Eagles are down to just four captains and need new guys to step up.

item.title: Watch Dani Pedrosa’s Spiked MotoGP Bike Beat an F1 Car, a Rally Car, a Pro 4 Truck and a Snowmobile on a 107-Acre Frozen Lake
item.description: Dani Pedrosa won the first Red Bull Ultimate Winter Race on a MotoGP bike with custom spiked wheels, beating an F1 car, a rally car, a Pro 4 truck and a snowmobile on a course built across 107 acres of frozen lake in Eagle River, Wisconsin, according to a Red Bull release dated November 12. Red Bull Media House sent the release with a 16-minute YouTube video, embedded below,. Temperatures on the lake were -17 degrees Celsius. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVScH48KGGA Video: Red Bull / YouTube The five entries Pedrosa rode a KTM RC16. Patrick Friesacher drove the F1 car, Scott Speed a Subaru WRX ARA 25, Andrew Carlson a Pro 4 truck and Gunnar Sterne a Ski-Doo 440 race sled, with Jeremiah Burton hosting. The release calls the F1 car “the Oracle Red Bull Racing car” and never gives a chassis. The video description names it as an RB7, the car Red Bull raced in 2011. Representative image: a 2011 Red Bull RB7. Photo: Calreyn88 / Wikimedia Commons (CC0) Speed is the lineup’s rally driver, in a sport where WRC has added Rally US to its 2027 calendar . Carlson’s truck is a V8 he puts at 950 horsepower in the video, and Red Bull has other off-road drivers on the payroll, such as Bryce Menzies, who we covered moving from Baja 1000 teammate to rival . How the course was set up The release says the track had shorter inside lines for the vehicles that don’t belong on ice and longer outside routes for the ones that do. Sterne, on the sled, ran the longest line. Carlson launched off a jump at the start. Every vehicle ran a calibration lap before the race. The video commentary says the five calibration laps landed within two seconds of each other, and that the rally car did its lap in 1:13. The sled carries about 400 studs and carbide skis; the commentators describe the MotoGP bike as having the largest spikes in the field and close to 300 horsepower. Friesacher says the F1 car got changes to tires and ride height for the cold, and that he would run longer spikes, like Pedrosa’s, next time. Representative image: a Pro 4 truck at Crandon, Wisconsin. Photo: Royalbroil / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0) The result Pedrosa credits the start. “My bike is one of the lightest vehicles, so I knew if I could gain a gap early, I could be more cautious through the turns,” he said in the release, adding that the tight turns made line choice the second key. The release says Friesacher finished “a close second” and gives no finishing order or times for anyone else. The video’s auto-generated captions are garbled at the finish and read as though the sled was second and the F1 car third, so we are only reporting what the release states. That aside, there’s a soccer game being played in Miami which is standing in for Haiti’s home match in the two leg Concacaf Nations League schedule this international window. As far as what to expect, the USA under Poch is pretty well established. It will try to dictate the match by moving the ball quickly up field and try to breakdown Haiti’s likely low block. The core of the team is back for this window and getting a win in the first leg will be key for the Americans. The Americans managed to score early and often both in the World Cup and in the recent friendlies. That habit will be useful against a team like Haiti who struggles to come back from falling behind or with keeping leads for that matter. A USA win should be in the cards for this one and if an early goal comes there may very well be more to follow.

item.title: NASCAR Fans Got Their Wish, But Ratings Still Plummeted Hard
item.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images NASCAR gave the fans exactly what they asked for, and the viewership numbers prove it did not work. The sanctioning body scrapped the “win and in” knockout-style format that had been in place for 12 seasons. Instead, they brought back an iteration of the “Chase” system used from 2004 to 2013, according to Beyond The Flag . Drivers, teams, and media outlets praised the move as a fix for the artificial drama of the old rules. Fans claimed they would return in droves once the “fake” championship battles were gone. Reality hit hard instead of the expected boom. Two of the early Chase races improved year over year, but the full 10-race postseason average finished down about 4 percent. Charlotte’s return to the oval was down roughly 15 percent from the prior Roval, while Kansas, Las Vegas, and Phoenix also posted declines. The Homestead finale itself was down 10.9 percent from the 2025 Phoenix championship race. The Numbers Do Not Lie Viewership fell even when the track layout changed to please the crowd. Even though the oval hosted the event for the first time since 2017, Charlotte Motor Speedway’s fall race drew roughly 15 percent fewer viewers than the previous year’s Roval event, while Kansas and Las Vegas also posted single-digit declines. Phoenix’s 2026 Chase race was down about 24 percent from the nearest comparable prior-year slot. Jeff Gluck observed that the decrease was fairly small given the title was effectively settled before the race concluded. Kyle Larson secured his third Cup Series title after the opening stage, leaving the rest of the field fighting only for pride. Excuses Fail to Explain the Decline To account for reduced TV figures, NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell cited rivalry from college football and the NFL. He emphasized that season-long race attendance grew 5%, while attendance for children aged 12 and under climbed 12%. This growth in the stands does not match the drop on the screen. The excuse of “football being on” does not explain the annual decline, even though college football has always been a factor. Bristol Motor Speedway’s night race fell 5.7%, and the convenient “college football” excuse was cited repeatedly. “But football was on!” does not explain an annual decline, as noted by Beyond The Flag. The sport lost 2% of its overall television viewership across the entire 2026 season. item.title: Hutton among trio to sign new Notts deals
item.description: Brett Hutton made his first-class debut for Nottinghamshire in 2011 [Shutterstock] Nottinghamshire seam bowler Brett Hutton is among a trio of players to sign new deals with the County Championship side. The 33-year-old, who was the club's leading wicket-taker with 38 when they won the Division One title in 2025, has agreed to remain at Trent Bridge until the end of the 2028 campaign. Hutton has spent 13 seasons with Nottinghamshire across two spells and has taken 357 wickets across all formats for them. Fellow seam bowler Tom Giles, 20, and 23-year-old all-rounder Ben Martindale have also extended their stays with the club, having both come though the academy as Hutton did more than a decade earlier. "I always want to keep making a difference for us in every facet of the game, and having been around the club for a while now, I also want to help the younger players coming through," Hutton told the club's website. "I've got the same hunger to perform and help this team achieve success that I've always had, and there's a great feeling among the strong group that we've got here at the moment." Giles, who has signed a new two-year deal, made his first-class debut for the club last season and went on to take five wickets in four County Championship appearances. Martindale, whose father Duncan also played for Nottinghamshire, has featured 32 times across all formats and has been a regular in the club's second XI side for a number of years. His new deal keeps him at Trent Bridge for a further 12 months.

item.title: Jalen Green Trade Rumors Heat Up As Suns Reportedly Seek Proven Point Guard
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Jalen Green scored 12 points against the Charlotte Hornets on Thursday, then watched the entire fourth quarter from the bench as Devin Booker closed out a 101–96 Phoenix Suns win. One rotation decision won’t determine Green’s future, but it captured how much his role has changed. The Suns once insisted Houston Rockets include him in the Kevin Durant trade. Now rival teams are wondering whether Phoenix would move him for a point guard. According to Sam Amick of The Athletic , the belief around the league is that the Suns are motivated to swap Green for a proven floor general. I want Jalen Green as a 23-year-old up-and-coming leading scorer.’” “They landed Green, of course, but that last part about him heading up their offensive efforts has simply not come to bear for these Suns (5-6). item.title: ‘The most comparable to Tom Brady’: Maxx Crosby says Joe Burrow is ‘the closest person we’ve seen’ to Tom Brady
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Over the past several years, Cincinnati Bengals superstar quarterback Joe Burrow has emerged as one of the top quarterbacks in the league. But longtime veteran star pass rusher Maxx Crosby wants everyone to know just how good he truly is. During a recent interview, Crosby said that if you “know ball,” you truly understand just how good Burrow is, as he went as far as to compare him to Tom Brady. Burrow’s Big Season Burrow and the Bengals are rolling right now. Cincinnati beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid last week to improve to 6-2, extending its winning streak to four games. Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions in the win, while also running in a touchdown. Ja’Marr Chase had 10 catches for 155 yards and a score, and Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns. Burrow’s 21 passing touchdowns lead the NFL. He also leads the league in completion percentage and is second in the league in passing yards, behind only Jordan Love. And he has been getting plenty of love lately. Earlier this week, ESPN’s Louis Riddick said on The Dan Patrick Show that Burrow is “that guy” and that there’s no other quarterback he would take over him. ‘The most comparable to Tom Brady’ Crosby discussed Burrow and Chase on the latest episode of his podcast, The Rush with Maxx Crosby . He made it clear he has been a Burrow believer for a long time. “He’s one of the best quarterbacks in the league. I’ve been saying that since, you know, since day one,” Crosby said. Then Crosby took it a step further. “So, yeah, if you know ball, you realize how good Joe Burrow is. He’s the most comparable, in my opinion. This is, and obviously there’s still levels and all that, but he’s the most comparable to Tom Brady in the way he plays in my eyes. I think he’s the closest person we’ve seen in that regard. Now, you got to go get seven of them, you know, to really be in that world. I’m sure of it, you know, but yeah, just the way he plays, the way he operates, and his pocket presence, I think, is the best thing about his game,” Crosby said. Crosby did have one piece of advice for Burrow, who has dealt with several injuries during his career. “Now, he takes some unnecessary blows. Even if you put a flag, even if he’s playing flag football, for some reason, Joe Burrow loves to take the worst spills of all time. If somebody can just get in there with [him] maybe and figure out how to land a little, like, more gracefully, I think would maybe do wonders for him,” Crosby continued. That’s high praise coming from one of the best pass rushers in the league.
